what_its_for: Primidone is used to control seizures (epilepsy). It may also be used to treat essential tremor, which is uncontrollable shaking of the hands or other parts of the body. It works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain.
how_to_take: Take primidone by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help if it upsets your stomach. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause serious problems including more seizures.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to find the right dose for you. Adults usually take 250 mg to 1,500 mg per day, divided into 3 or 4 doses. Children under 8 years old usually take 125 mg to 750 mg per day in divided doses. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions because your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss several doses, call your doctor for guidance.
storage: Store primidone at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking primidone, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines — including over-the-counter drugs and supplements — without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, because many medicines can interact with primidone. Avoid stopping this medicine suddenly without your doctor's approval.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of hurting yourself or suicide, severe depression or mood changes, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing, unusual eye movements, vision changes, loss of coordination, or extreme drowsiness, signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain, or if your seizures get worse or change in any way.
when_it_works: Primidone starts working within a few days, but it may take several weeks to reach the right dose and for you to get the full benefit. Do not stop taking it just because you feel better — this medicine only works if you take it regularly every day.
special_populations: Older adults (seniors): You may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, drowsiness, and confusion. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose to reduce these risks. Pregnant women: Primidone may harm an unborn baby, but stopping seizure medicine during pregnancy can also be dangerous. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before making any changes. Use reliable birth control while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding mothers: Primidone passes into breast milk and may cause drowsiness or feeding problems in nursing babies. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Primidone can sometimes cause opposite effects in children, such as hyperactivity or excitement instead of drowsiness. Let your doctor know if you notice unusual behavior changes in your child. Kidney or liver disease: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver problems.
